issues.title: Missing router import causes undefined variable error in BookerWebWrapper
issues.description: The `useRouter` hook is removed from the imports but the `router` variable is still used in multiple places within the component (lines 193, 228, 233, 239). This will cause a ReferenceError at runtime when any of these code paths are executed, such as when toggling the overlay calendar, navigating for instant meetings, or handling calendar interactions. The router is critical for navigation functionality in the booking flow.

issues.title: Incorrect priority sorting in sortHosts breaks round-robin host assignment
issues.description: The priority comparison logic is inverted when weights are equal in round-robin mode. The code now returns `priorityA - priorityB` instead of `priorityB - priorityA`, which sorts hosts in ascending priority order (lowest priority first) instead of descending (highest priority first). This causes lower-priority hosts to be selected before higher-priority hosts when weights are equal, breaking the intended assignment logic throughout the application wherever host assignment is used.

issues.title: Missing module resolution in dynamic import causes team assignment tab to fail
issues.description: The EventTeamAssignmentTab dynamic import is missing the `.then((mod) => mod)` module resolution that all other tab imports use. This inconsistency will cause the dynamic import to not properly extract the default export, resulting in the team assignment tab failing to render correctly. When users navigate to the team assignment tab for event types, they will encounter a blank screen or rendering error because the component cannot be properly loaded.

pr.title: Code Review Bench PR #26629 - refactor: move WebWrapper files from packages/platform to apps/web/modules

structured_output.summary:
This PR moves the web-only `*WebWrapper` components out of `packages/platform/atoms` and into `apps/web` (event-type tabs, Booker, conferencing, selected/destination calendars, add-members). Imports that used to cross packages now point at siblings. It also moves `sortHosts` into `@calcom/lib/bookings/hostGroupUtils` and exposes three event-type hooks through `@calcom/atoms` package exports.

It's billed as a pure move, but there are real regressions. `BookerWebWrapper` dropped the `useRouter()` call while still using `router` in several places, so every booking page will throw a ReferenceError on render. The `sortHosts` move flipped the tie-break order when weights are enabled. Several atoms files still point at the deleted files: `booker/export.ts`, the `ConferencingAppsViewPlatformWrapper` type import, and the stale `./booker` package export. That breaks type-check and the atoms build. There are also leftovers like a deep relative import across packages, broken indentation, and a missing newline at end of file.
structured_output.verdictRationale: `BookerWebWrapper` references an undeclared `router`, which will crash every public booking page. `sortHosts` silently changed its sort order. Several files in `packages/platform/atoms` still import modules this PR moved, so the type-check the PR itself recommends will fail.

architecture.overview:
Before this PR, `apps/web` pages imported web-specific wrappers (EventTypeWebWrapper, BookerWebWrapper, ConferencingAppsViewWebWrapper, SelectedCalendars and DestinationCalendar wrappers, AddMembersWithSwitchWebWrapper) from `@calcom/atoms`. Those wrappers then imported back into `@calcom/web/modules/...`, which made a cross-package cycle.

The PR moves the wrappers into `apps/web` next to the components they wrap, so imports become sibling-relative. `@calcom/atoms` keeps the platform wrappers and shared hooks. It now exports `useEventTypeForm`, `useHandleRouteChange`, `useTabsNavigations` and `SelectedCalendarsSettings` so `apps/web` can still use them. `sortHosts` moves from a UI file into `@calcom/lib`, so the atoms hook no longer depends on `apps/web`.
steps: Start with the Next.js routes and views (`event-types/[type]/page.tsx`, the `team/type-view*` and `users-type-public-view` booking views, the conferencing settings page). They now import wrappers from `@calcom/web/modules/...` instead of `@calcom/atoms`.

`apps/web/modules/event-types/components/EventTypeWebWrapper.tsx` dynamically loads tab wrappers from `./tabs/*/` and pulls the form, route-change and tab hooks from `@calcom/atoms/event-types/hooks/*`.
`apps/web/modules/bookings/components/BookerWebWrapper.tsx` wraps the sibling `./Booker` component and handles navigation for the overlay calendar and instant meetings.
The calendar settings wrappers (`modules/calendars/components/SelectedCalendarsSettingsWebWrapper`, `components/apps/DestinationCalendarSettingsWebWrapper`) still render atoms base components.
`packages/lib/bookings/hostGroupUtils.ts` now owns `sortHosts`. It's used by `HostEditDialogs`, `EventTeamAssignmentTab` and the atoms `useEventTypeForm` hook.

`packages/platform/atoms/package.json` exports drop the web wrappers and add the hook and SelectedCalendarsSettings entries. Files left in atoms (`booker/export.ts`, `ConferencingAppsViewPlatformWrapper`) still point at the moved files.

findings.title: `router` is used but `useRouter()` was removed, so every booking page crashes
findings.fixPrompt: In `apps/web/modules/bookings/components/BookerWebWrapper.tsx`, the move removed `useRouter` from the `next/navigation` import (line 4) and deleted `const router = useRouter();` at the top of `BookerWebWrapperComponent` (around line 41). `router` is still used in `onOverlaySwitchStateChange` (lines ~193-195), `onConnectNowInstantMeeting`, `onOverlayClickNoCalendar` and `onClickOverlayContinue`. Re-add `useRouter` to the import and declare `const router = useRouter();` as the first line of `BookerWebWrapperComponent`, before `usePathname()`. Leave `useRef` removed; it's unused.

findings.title: `sortHosts` tie-break order was flipped during the move
findings.fixPrompt: In `packages/lib/bookings/hostGroupUtils.ts`, `sortHosts` (lines 41-60) was moved from `apps/web/modules/event-types/components/HostEditDialogs.tsx`, but the equal-weight tie-break was changed from `priorityB - priorityA` to `priorityA - priorityB`. Restore `priorityB - priorityA` so behavior matches the original. Add unit tests next to the existing hostGroupUtils tests (or create `hostGroupUtils.test.ts`) covering: weights enabled with different weights, weights enabled with equal weights and different priorities, weights disabled, and null weight/priority defaults (100 and 2).

findings.title: Atoms files still import the moved/deleted files (booker export, conferencing types, `./booker` export)
findings.body:
Some files left in `packages/platform/atoms` still reference modules this PR moved or deleted:

- `packages/platform/atoms/booker/export.ts` still runs `export { BookerWebWrapper as Booker } from "./BookerWebWrapper";`, and that file no longer exists.
- `packages/platform/atoms/connect/conferencing-apps/ConferencingAppsViewPlatformWrapper.tsx` (lines 27-30) imports the `BulkUpdatParams` and `UpdateUsersDefaultConferencingAppParams` types from `./ConferencingAppsViewWebWrapper`, which was moved to `apps/web`. That file is part of the public atoms entry (`index.ts:34`), so the dts build and `yarn type-check:ci` will fail.
- `package.json` still declares `"./booker": "./booker/index.ts"`, but this PR deletes `booker/index.ts`. Any consumer of `@calcom/atoms/booker` will get a module-not-found error instead of a clean removal.

::diff{file="packages/platform/atoms/package.json" lines="56-59"}

::callout{type="warning"}
The types used by the platform wrapper should live in atoms (e.g. a `connect/conferencing-apps/types.ts`). The web wrapper should import them from there, not the other way around, or the cross-package dependency comes back.
findings.fixPrompt: After moving the web wrappers out of `packages/platform/atoms`, three references are dangling. (1) Remove the `"./booker": "./booker/index.ts"` entry in `packages/platform/atoms/package.json` (line ~58), since `booker/index.ts` was deleted. (2) Delete `packages/platform/atoms/booker/export.ts` or fix it; it re-exports from the deleted `./BookerWebWrapper`. Confirm nothing references it. (3) In `packages/platform/atoms/connect/conferencing-apps/ConferencingAppsViewPlatformWrapper.tsx` (lines 27-30), the types `BulkUpdatParams` and `UpdateUsersDefaultConferencingAppParams` come from the moved `./ConferencingAppsViewWebWrapper`. Move those type definitions into a new atoms file (e.g. `connect/conferencing-apps/types.ts`). Import them from there in the platform wrapper and in `apps/web/modules/apps/components/ConferencingAppsViewWebWrapper.tsx` (re-export them if needed). Then run `yarn type-check:ci --force`.

findings.title: Deep relative imports into `packages/platform/atoms` instead of the package alias
findings.body:
The moved `DestinationCalendarSettingsWebWrapper` reaches into the atoms package with filesystem-relative paths:

::diff{file="apps/web/components/apps/DestinationCalendarSettingsWebWrapper.tsx" lines="1-4"}

That skips the package boundary and `exports` map, and it breaks if either directory moves. The PR description says the same kind of import was fixed in `EventTypeWebWrapper` via the `@calcom/atoms` alias, so this one looks like an oversight. The PR also says the file goes to `apps/web/modules/...`, but it actually landed in `apps/web/components/apps/`, which doesn't match the other wrappers.

Add `./destination-calendar/DestinationCalendar` and `./src/components/atoms-wrapper` entries to the atoms `package.json` exports, as was done for `SelectedCalendarsSettings`, and import through `@calcom/atoms/...`.
findings.fixPrompt: `apps/web/components/apps/DestinationCalendarSettingsWebWrapper.tsx` lines 3-4 import `AtomsWrapper` and `DestinationCalendarSettings` via `../../../../packages/platform/atoms/...` relative paths. Add export entries in `packages/platform/atoms/package.json` for `./destination-calendar/DestinationCalendar` and `./src/components/atoms-wrapper` (or reuse existing ones if present), then switch these imports to `@calcom/atoms/...`. You could also move the file to `apps/web/modules/calendars/components/` next to `SelectedCalendarsSettingsWebWrapper`, and update the import in `apps/web/components/apps/CalendarListContainer.tsx`.

findings.title: Formatting noise: broken JSX indentation, missing EOF newlines, unsorted imports
findings.body:
A few unrelated formatting changes slipped in. The `setup` and `availability` entries in `tabMap` switched to 8-space/4-space indentation, while the rest of the map uses the usual 2-space Prettier style:

::diff{file="apps/web/modules/event-types/components/EventTypeWebWrapper.tsx" lines="234-251"}

Also:
- `EventLimitsTabWebWrapper.tsx` and `EventRecurringWebWrapper.tsx` lost their trailing newline.
- Those same two files still import themselves' siblings through `@calcom/web/modules/...` instead of the relative imports used everywhere else in this PR.
- The `@calcom/atoms/...` imports in `EventTypeWebWrapper.tsx` (lines 29-31) come after the relative imports, and `AddMembersWithSwitch.tsx`/`CalendarListContainer.tsx` put a relative import in the middle of the `@calcom/*` block.

Running Prettier and the import sorter on the touched files should fix all of it.
findings.fixPrompt: Run Prettier and the repo's import-sort config on the files touched by this PR. Specifically: re-indent the `setup` and `availability` JSX in `tabMap` in `apps/web/modules/event-types/components/EventTypeWebWrapper.tsx` (lines 234-251) to 2-space style; restore trailing newlines in `tabs/limits/EventLimitsTabWebWrapper.tsx` and `tabs/recurring/EventRecurringWebWrapper.tsx` and switch their imports to relative `./EventLimitsTab` / `./EventRecurringTab`; move the `@calcom/atoms/...` imports in `EventTypeWebWrapper.tsx` (lines 29-31) up with the other `@calcom` imports; and group the relative imports in `AddMembersWithSwitch.tsx` and `CalendarListContainer.tsx` after the package imports.

findings.title: Moving `sortHosts` into `@calcom/lib` removes a real dependency inversion
findings.body: Before this PR, the atoms `useEventTypeForm` hook imported `sortHosts` from a React dialog file in `apps/web`. That made a package depend on the app. Putting the function in `packages/lib/bookings/hostGroupUtils.ts` next to `groupHostsByGroupId` is the right home, and all three call sites now use it. Apart from the tie-break regression above, this is a good cleanup.
